title: Read restrictions: overlapping column projections on nested types
summary: This part of the thread deals with what should happen when read restrictions returned by a catalog place projections on both a nested container and one of its descendants. Sung Yun withdrew an earlier claim that relaxing a disallow rule later would be fully backward-compatible, and shared a survey of existing systems: each resolves to a single policy per field value, none composes several masking transforms, and most make ancestor-descendant overlap impossible to author. Russell Spitzer pointed to the precedent of nested default values (PR #12841), where the ambiguous configuration was simply disallowed, and supported Option A: catalogs must not emit overlapping nested projections and readers must fail closed. Daniel Weeks, who had wanted a more opinionated stance on the conflict, said he was fine with putting the complexity on the catalog and disallowing overlap. Prashant Singh updated the spec PR with that conclusion.

positions.stance: Option A fits how existing policy engines behave, since surveyed systems resolve to one policy per field value; relaxing the rule later would not be fully backward-compatible.
Follow the default-values precedent and disallow the ambiguous state: catalogs must not emit overlapping nested projections and readers must fail closed.
Would also have accepted a defined application order, but is fine with the catalog deconflicting or failing and overlap being disallowed.

outcome.note: Overlapping projections on a nested type and its descendants are disallowed, with expectations on both the catalog and the client side; the spec PR was updated accordingly.

why_it_matters: Catalogs must resolve nested policy conflicts themselves, and clients reject overlapping projections instead of implementing precedence rules.
